title: Consider moving the definition of "user agent" to the TAG user-agents document
body:
### What is the issue with the Infra Standard?

Infra defines the term "user agent": https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#user-agent

The TAG is working on a Note that refines this definition a bit (https://www.w3.org/TR/web-user-agents/#what), and also adopts the "duties" that the W3C Privacy Principles ascribed to user agents.

So far, we've marked the definition `noexport` in order to avoid citation conflicts, but clearly we want a single shared definition in the long run. How does the Infra community feel about moving the canonical definition to a TAG-owned document?

@marcoscaceres raised a question about the normative status of the definition. The TAG document is a [Note](https://www.w3.org/policies/process/#note-track), and maybe eventually a Statement. Those kinds of documents don't make normative requirements, and don't gather patent commitments. Infra is a normative document. This would be a problem if the TAG document required user agents to follow particular algorithms. I think it's not a problem in this case because the TAG document is just defining a kind of entity, and only Recommendations and WHATWG Standards will normatively require those entities to do things. But my opinion doesn't make anything true.

How do y'all think we should proceed? Is it ok for web specs in general to depend on a TAG note for this, or should we find a way to publish a normative document?
